why: When the wgpu host's presentation ladder is declared STALLED, and what it does about it. `AppPresenter::admit_next_frame` refuses to build a frame while `has_pending_presentation()`, so a presentation cursor that stops advancing stops the whole host: no frame transaction, no runtime mailbox pump, no world snapshot apply, no retained document ingress, no accessibility projection. Measured on 6118 as `os_host frame gate blocked=true pending=true phase=Some(Engine)` held from t≈85 s to t≈200 s and as `phase=Some(Aborted) retained-fault=true` (ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END, `📓️wgpu-wheel-zoom-a11y-live-2026-09-14.md` §3.4, `📓️wgpu-host-settle-pump-2026-09-14.md` §7). The watchdog counts CONSECUTIVE non-advancing `Pending` answers over the cursor's own progress signature — phase, engine packet index, upload page index, and whether a GPU cursor is held — so a legitimately long presentation resets on every index it moves and only a frozen cursor accumulates. On the ceiling step it names the holder once and aborts the presentation, which is the one action that reopens the gate without touching a GPU owner. The signature also carries the GPU present cursor's OWN (phase, command, glass command, glass-foreground command, blur mip): `AppPresentPhase::Render` holds one `gpu_cursor` for a whole composite pass, so without the inner five the outer shape is frozen for as many steps as the scene has commands and the watchdog aborts a healthy present — measured on 6118 as `os_host present stalled phase=Render engine=1 upload=1 gpu-cursor=true` at t≈4.4 s on EVERY example boot. EVERY cursor the ladder walks has to be in there: the `ForegroundCommands` walk was added without its index and quarantined the surface 13 770 pages into a perfectly healthy present (ticket 26/09/17/WGPU-RENDERER-REACT-PARITY). The fifth term is the WITHIN-ITEM upload progress `(mesh vertex, mesh index, atlas page)`: `AppPresentCursor::upload` only moves when a whole upload item completes and one mesh item is written one vertex per step, so a healthy mesh upload froze the outer shape for as many steps as the mesh has vertices and the host's own gate census could only report `phase=Some(Uploads) … stall-steps=293` with no reason attached (ticket 26/09/17/WGPU-RENDERER-REACT-PARITY, `📓️w11a-prepared-world-mesh-missing.md`).

cases.why: A healthy ladder moves an index on every step and is never reported, however long it runs.

A composite pass whose OUTER shape never moves while its GPU cursor encodes command after command is healthy and must never be reported — the false positive a signature without the inner four produces on every boot.

One mesh upload item is written ONE VERTEX PER STEP, so the outer `upload` index is frozen for the whole walk. The within-item counters are what keep the watchdog armed without quarantining a perfectly healthy 293-vertex mesh.
A mesh upload that stops writing IS a stall, and the within-item counters are what name where it stopped.
The measured wedge: `realize_step` answering `Ok(false)` forever with the engine packet index frozen. Reported once, on the ceiling step, and never again.
The second measured variant: an `Aborted` cursor whose close never completes.
A GPU cursor that itself freezes mid-composite IS a stall, and the inner four are what name it.

The glass-foreground walk: `ForegroundCommands` (phase 6) re-walks every measured command page to re-encode the content a glass region carries on its face, and moves ONLY its own index. Without that index in the signature this healthy walk is reported as a stall and the surface is quarantined — measured on 6213 as `worker-present-failed: presentation stalled: phase=Render engine=0 upload=1 gpu-cursor=Some((6, 13770, 13770, 5))` on every boot (ticket 26/09/17/WGPU-RENDERER-REACT-PARITY).
